::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [21 August 1866]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Westcountry Studies Library, Exeter/ Yonge 1866/2
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd)
Thank you for the Acrostic, but I had decided on leaving that field to the [Magazine for the Young](organizations/other_79.qmd), which always has a batch of Acrostics at Christmas.[^1] I have so often refused them on that score that I could not take these. We guessed all except the two Es, which I do not quite understand, unless it means Edward and Elizabeth - and for Idiot too we had to go to the answer.

yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: In envelope addressed to Miss Smith/ 8 Wellington Road/ Old Charlton/ SE and postmarked Winchester 20 August and London SE 21 August 1866.
[^2]: In fact the *Magazine for the Young* was increasingly making a feature of acrostics, not just at Christmas but throughout the year.
